title: Context-aware authorization runtime + policy decision service (PDP) for RBAC v2
creator: Marco Li
description: Build a context-aware Policy Decision Point (PDP) service and lightweight authorization middleware to replace the ad-hoc RBAC checks across API, runtime, and Console. The goal is to centralize policy evaluation, provide deterministic audit events, and enable fine-grained admin controls and SSO/SAML mapping sync for RBAC v2. This ticket covers design, a reference implementation of the PDP, middleware adapters for HTTP/gRPC and runtime request paths, audit schema, and a phased rollout plan to Dedicated and Private deployments.
acceptance_criteria: PDP service accepts canonical request context (actor, resource, action, metadata) and returns allow/deny + obligations within 50ms P95 for 95% of requests in local perf tests
Authorization middleware unified across API, runtime worker, and Console with identical decision semantics
Structured audit events emitted for every decision with correlation id and policy version, stored in the audit log sink (S3 + Elastic)
SSO/SAML attribute mappings can be ingested and materialized as attributes in PDP decisions within 60s of change
Canary rollout to 10% of API traffic with automatic fallback to legacy checks on errors
End-to-end tests validate deny-by-default, escalation prevention for admin actions, and attribute-based exceptions
tasks: Design PDP API contract and canonical request context (security-team + runtime-team)
Implement reference PDP with compiled policy trees and fast-path cache
Write authorization middleware adapters: http-authz (API), grpc-authz (runtime), console-plugin-authz
Define audit event schema and wire up to existing audit sink; include policy_version and evaluation_trace
Create SAML/SCIM sync job changes to emit mapping deltas to PDP
Build canary config in router to route to new PDP and measure error budgets
Add observability: per-policy latencies, cache-hit ratios, denied-by-policy breakdowns
Author docs for SDKs and migration guide for teams using legacy inline checks
decision_log: 2026-02-22: Chose a PDP + thin middleware model (vs sidecar) to minimize runtime surface area and simplify deployments across Hosted/Dedicated/Private
2026-02-25: Agreed to use compiled policy trees with stable versioning to ensure deterministic audit traces
2026-03-01: Opted for synchronous PDP check on control-plane/admin operations, but asynchronous advisory checks for non-critical telemetry to avoid p95 regressions
2026-03-05: Decided to represent obligations as JSON-encoded actions to allow middleware to issue audit-only telemetry or trigger follow-up workflows

2026-02-27 - Asha Patel: Started a prototype of the compiled policy tree. Cache invalidation semantics are the main open question — pushing a doc later today.
2026-03-03 - Jordan Kim: Runtime team will need a lightweight library (no network) to evaluate local allowlists for extreme-latency paths. Proposal: ship fallback rules as a signed policy bundle.
2026-03-08 - Security Review Bot: preliminary scan passed; scheduled manual review with cryptography team on 2026-03-15
notes: Blockers: policy compiler needs an extra optimization pass to avoid pathological tree blowups on attribute-heavy rules. Also need an SSO attribute privacy checklist before materializing certain attributes into PDP. Next milestone is a working prototype and perf benchmarks in staging by 2026-03-20.
